BiblicalUsage: Gahar means to bow down low, to stretch oneself out flat. Elijah cast himself down upon the earth on Carmel and put his face between his knees in 1 Kings 18:42, waiting for rain. Elisha went up and stretched himself upon the dead child in 2 Kings 4:34, mouth to mouth and hands to hands, until the flesh waxed warm, and in 2 Kings 4:35 he stretched himself upon him again, and the child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe bowing low is the posture of power in God's kingdom. Elijah bowed on Carmel and the rain came; Elisha stretched himself over a dead boy and life returned. I hold that God works through those willing to get low.
